rendered: The document does not support the premise. Prestraining did not lower the Li-ion diffusion coefficient of the V2O5 films; it raised it. The diffusion coefficient in the strained state increased to about 2.5-times[1] the value for the unstrained state. The authors' proposed mechanism is volumetric: an out-of-plane compressive strain produces in-plane tensile strains that effectively increase the total volume of the crystal. They also suggest that the increase could be due to a reduction of ion migration barriers imposed by mechanical strains, though this is inferred from earlier simulation reports rather than shown directly.[2][3][4]
